change: Strengthened the live prompt and added a deterministic professional-plausibility gate for distractors.

activity.title: Managing Scope and Stakeholder Expectations
activity.situation: You are leading a cross-functional delivery team and need to respond to a stakeholder request that threatens current project boundaries. You must handle this through scope negotiation.
activity.sentence_template: Regarding the latest feature additions, we can proceed by {blank_1}, provided that we maintain {blank_2}, and schedule a review with {blank_3}.

options.text: integrating the core items into the next sprint
our current delivery velocity and quality standards
the steering committee next Tuesday morning
accepting all change requests immediately without re-estimating
deferring stakeholder alignment until the final release phase

o1.why: This option clearly defines an actionable step that fits naturally into the workflow without committing to unrealistic timelines.

o2.why: This option protects critical delivery parameters while remaining constructive to stakeholder needs.

o3.why: This option identifies a specific governance forum and timeframe, ensuring appropriate oversight.

o4.what_to_improve: Ensure change requests are formally evaluated against capacity rather than accepted unconditionally.
o4.why: While proactive in tone, accepting all requests without re-estimation risks team burnout and scope creep.

o5.what_to_improve: Involve stakeholders earlier to prevent misaligned expectations later in the delivery lifecycle.
o5.why: Deferring alignment until the final stage creates a high risk of late-stage rework and stakeholder dissatisfaction.

strengths: The scenario accurately captures the delicate balance required when managing scope creep and communicating trade-offs to stakeholders.
The target sentence reads coherently and naturally once completed with the intended options.
Feedback explanations are supportive, objective, and clearly articulate the strategic implications of each approach without using punitive phrasing.

issues.explanation: Both distractors (o4 and o5) rely on gerund phrases starting with verbs ('accepting...', 'deferring...'), which primarily make them syntactic candidates for blank_1 rather than blanks 2 or 3.
issues.recommended_fix: Consider varying the syntactic form of one distractor so that it presents a plausible alternative for blank_2 or blank_3, such as a noun phrase reflecting poor delivery metrics.

judge_review.summary: This is a well-structured and realistic activity for a delivery lead negotiating scope. The sentence structure is coherent, the options are distinct, and the feedback provided is constructive and educational.

responsibilities: Coordinated on-call response and mentored junior staff

activity.title: Critical Outage Escalation Communication
activity.situation: As an experienced network and systems administrator coordinating an on-call response while mentoring junior staff, you need to inform senior stakeholders about a major infrastructure incident affecting core services, outlining the immediate mitigation steps and the planned restoration schedule.
activity.sentence_template: During the recent critical outage escalation, {blank_1} to stabilise the core routing infrastructure, while {blank_2} alongside the junior engineers to ensure knowledge transfer, and {blank_3} to provide a transparent progress report.

options.text: we immediately implemented the secondary BGP failover paths
I guided the team through systematic log analysis
we committed to delivering hourly status updates
we temporarily bypassed all standard change control protocols
I handled every diagnostic task independently

o1.why: This accurately highlights the technical action taken to address the critical outage escalation.

o2.why: This effectively reflects your mentoring responsibilities while actively managing the incident response.

o3.why: This establishes clear stakeholder expectations regarding communication during a high-priority event.

o4.what_to_improve: Ensure governance procedures are maintained even under pressure, as bypassing change control entirely introduces operational risk.
o4.why: Bypassing formal protocols entirely can lead to undocumented configuration drift and secondary incidents.

o5.what_to_improve: Delegate appropriate diagnostic tasks to junior staff to support their professional development during live incidents.
o5.why: Handling everything independently misses an opportunity for mentorship and can overwhelm the lead administrator.

strengths: The scenario accurately reflects the operational balance between technical mitigation and mentoring during incident response.
The intended options assemble into an articulate, grammatically fluent update suitable for senior stakeholders.
The feedback clearly articulates the operational risks of bypassing change management and failing to delegate.

issues.explanation: If option o5 ('I handled every diagnostic task independently') is placed into blank_2, it creates a slight semantic contradiction with the following clause ('alongside the junior engineers').
issues.recommended_fix: Consider rephrasing option o5 slightly, for example to 'I focused on troubleshooting critical services without direct input', to keep the contrast natural without directly clashing with the adjacent phrase.

judge_review.summary: This is a well-designed activity that convincingly captures the communicative and mentoring challenges faced by senior technical administrators during major incidents.
